title: The Company 3-Way Diagram: Legal vs. Illegal Wiring

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Training wall with two identical 3-way boards, labeled Board 1 and Board 2. Matthew holds the company 3-way reference sheet. Medium shot.
scenes.on_screen: The Company 3-Way Diagram: Legal vs. Illegal
scenes.says: This one sheet in our training folder could save your life. It shows the same two switches and one light wired two ways, one marked LEGAL and one marked ILLEGAL. Here's the point: a three-way circuit can work perfectly and still be wired wrong, and dangerous. Never trust a wall switch as your disconnect. This diagram is the reason.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Close-up of Board 1 with diagram overlay tracing hot, travelers, switch leg, neutral.
scenes.on_screen: LEGAL: hot to a common | 2 travelers | other common to lamp | neutral straight to lamp
scenes.says: Board one, the legal way. Line hot lands on the common of one switch. Two travelers run between the traveler terminals and carry only the hot. The other switch's common feeds the lamp. And the neutral goes straight to the lamp. It's never connected to a switch terminal. When the light is off, the fixture is disconnected from the hot.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Close-up of Board 2 with diagram overlay: hot and neutral on traveler terminals, lamp between the two commons.
scenes.on_screen: ILLEGAL: hot AND neutral on the travelers, lamp between the commons
scenes.says: Board two, the illegal way. Hot and neutral are both brought to the traveler terminals, and the lamp sits between the two commons. Each switch picks hot or neutral for its side of the lamp. Different picks, the lamp lights. Same pick, it goes out. It switches from both places, so the customer never complains.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Both boards light and switch normally as instructor flips switches.
scenes.on_screen: Both boards work. Only one is safe.
scenes.says: Watch. Both boards light. Both switch from either location. You can't tell them apart by flipping switches.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Board 2 switched off; non-contact tester held at the lamp socket lights and beeps. Close-up.
scenes.says: Now both switches on the hot traveler. The lamp is dark, but the socket shell, the lamp base and the fixture wiring are all at line voltage. A tech who turns off the switch to change a lamp can be shocked. That's why it's illegal: the NEC requires switching in the hot only, 404.2(A), and doesn't let a switch disconnect the neutral, 404.2(B).

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.on_screen: Non-contact tester = warning, not diagnosis. LOTO + live-dead-live at the fixture.
scenes.says: Safety. Before touching a lamp, socket or fixture on any three-way circuit, lock out and tag out the breaker and verify absence of voltage, live-dead-live, at the fixture, testing each conductor to ground. A non-contact tester lighting up with the switch off is a warning, not a diagnosis. Stop and verify with a meter.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Close-up of a mock-up box: a white source conductor landing on a traveler terminal.
scenes.on_screen: Clues: white from source on a traveler | lamp between two switch legs | fixture neutral traces to a switch
scenes.says: How you spot it: a non-contact alert at an off fixture, a white from the source landing on a traveler terminal, a lamp connected between two switch legs with no neutral splice. Your tool is the de-energized continuity trace from lessons two and three. Don't work energized to prove it. And remember, colors vary. Wire color proves nothing.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Tech locks out the training panel feeding Board 2, photographs the labeled wiring, writes on a work order.
scenes.on_screen: 1 Stop, leave it locked out  2 Tell your lead, photograph  3 Write it up  4 Tell the customer
scenes.says: What you do: stop and leave the circuit locked out. Tell your lead or supervisor and photograph the wiring with every conductor labeled. Write it up: neutral switched, fixture energized with switches off, needs rewiring to code. Tell the customer the fixture is hazardous to service from the switch, and don't leave without it documented.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Matthew holding the reference sheet, medium shot.
scenes.on_screen: LT2 recognizes. LT3+ troubleshoots. Code violations: write it up.
scenes.says: At LT2 you learn to recognize both versions. LT3 and up troubleshoot three-way circuits unsupervised, and correcting a violation like this may need an electrician, depending on whether new conductors are needed. Now read the lesson and take the quiz.
